tools.name: qumo_run_qasm
tools.description:
Use when you need measurement counts of a circuit or a program with mid-circuit measurement or while loops.
Instead or first: qumo_statevector for exact amplitudes, qumo_expectation for <H>, qumo_emulate for a device's noise.
Watch out: counts are bitstrings with the leftmost character as the highest qubit; set seed for reproducible runs.

Simulate an OpenQASM 2/3 circuit or program and return measurement counts (Qiskit-style bitstrings, leftmost = highest bit). Deterministic for a given seed. Circuits without measurements are measured on all qubits. Supports mid-circuit measurement, reset, feed-forward and '#pragma qumo' noise (per-shot trajectories), and while, break, continue and classical variables, shot by shot: those results add 'iterations' (back-edges per shot) and 'outputs' (declared output variables).

qasm.description: (required unless circuit is given) OpenQASM 3.0 or 2.0 source, e.g. 'OPENQASM 3.0; include "stdgates.inc"; qubit[2] q; bit[2] c; h q[0]; cx q[0], q[1]; c = measure q;'

circuit.description: Alternative to qasm: circuit JSON in format qumo.circuit.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

program.description: Alternative to qasm: program JSON in format qumo.program.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

params.description: Values for 'input float' parameters: array in declaration order or object name->value

max_qubits.description: Safety limit for dense simulation (16*2^n bytes)

max_iterations.description: Loop back-edges allowed per shot; past it the run stops with QM-E480

tools.name: qumo_statevector
tools.description:
Use when you need exact amplitudes (small circuits, debugging, checking an algorithm).
Instead or first: qumo_run_qasm when only counts matter.
Watch out: memory grows as 2^n; respect max_qubits.

Return the exact final state vector (amplitudes with probability > threshold, sorted by basis index) of a unitary circuit. Measurements and resets are ignored; classically-conditioned gates are rejected (QM-E401), and so is a program with runtime control flow (QM-E585).

qasm.description: (required unless circuit is given) OpenQASM 3.0 or 2.0 source, e.g. 'OPENQASM 3.0; include "stdgates.inc"; qubit[2] q; bit[2] c; h q[0]; cx q[0], q[1]; c = measure q;'

circuit.description: Alternative to qasm: circuit JSON in format qumo.circuit.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

params.description: Values for 'input float' parameters: array in declaration order or object name->value

tools.name: qumo_expectation
tools.description:
Use when you need an exact expectation value of a Pauli-sum observable, e.g. '0.5*Z0 Z1 - 1.2*X0'.
Watch out: observable syntax is coefficient*Pauli+index terms separated by + or -.

Exact expectation value <psi|H|psi> of a Pauli-sum observable (e.g. '0.5*Z0 Z1 - 1.2*X0 + 0.3' or dense 'ZZI') on the circuit's final state. Pass an array of observables to evaluate several at once. A program with runtime control flow has no single final state: QM-E585.

qasm.description: (required unless circuit is given) OpenQASM 3.0 or 2.0 source, e.g. 'OPENQASM 3.0; include "stdgates.inc"; qubit[2] q; bit[2] c; h q[0]; cx q[0], q[1]; c = measure q;'

circuit.description: Alternative to qasm: circuit JSON in format qumo.circuit.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

observable.description: Pauli sum string, or array of strings

params.description: Values for 'input float' parameters: array in declaration order or object name->value

tools.name: qumo_validate_qasm
tools.description:
Use when you wrote or received OpenQASM and want parse errors and lint before running anything.
Instead or first: always run it first on hand-written or user-supplied QASM.
Watch out: it does not simulate; errors carry QM-E5xx codes with line and column.

Parse and lint OpenQASM 2/3 without simulating, including programs with while and classical variables. Returns valid=true/false, structured errors (stable QM-Exxx code, message, line, col, snippet, hint) and lint warnings (QM-Wxxx), plus a summary when valid.

qasm.description: (required unless circuit is given) OpenQASM 3.0 or 2.0 source, e.g. 'OPENQASM 3.0; include "stdgates.inc"; qubit[2] q; bit[2] c; h q[0]; cx q[0], q[1]; c = measure q;'

tools.name: qumo_describe
tools.description:
Use when you need facts about QUMO itself: gate list and syntax, an error code's meaning and fix, capabilities, compiler passes or AI models.
Instead or first: call it before guessing a gate name, a pass name or what an error code means.
Watch out: topic is required in practice: 'gates', 'gate'+name, 'errors', 'error'+name (e.g. QM-E506), 'capabilities', 'passes', 'models'.

Machine-readable self-description: topic 'gates' (every gate: arity, params, Clifford/diagonal flags, QASM syntax, matrix), 'gate' + name, 'errors' (error-code catalog with fix hints; format 'markdown' returns docs/ERRORS.md), 'error' + name (one code), 'capabilities' (simulators, QASM subset, conventions, tools), 'passes' (compiler pass catalog incl. the AI synthesis passes, route AI keys and presets) or 'models' (installed AI-transpiler models from the INDEX.json registries; 'name' = optional model directory).

name.description: Gate name/alias or error code for topic gate/error; model directory for topic models

tools.name: qumo_circuit_info
tools.description:
Use when you need size facts without simulating: qubits, depth, gate counts, 2-qubit gates, lint.
Instead or first: use before choosing a simulator, or to report a circuit's cost.

Analyze a circuit without simulating: qubits, clbits, op counts, depth, two-qubit gate count, T-count, Clifford/dynamic/noisy flags, parameters, memory estimate, recommended simulator and lint findings. Optionally include the instruction list (JSON) and canonical OpenQASM 3. A program with runtime control flow gets blocks, loops, variables and cost per loop instead of a depth.

qasm.description: (required unless circuit is given) OpenQASM 3.0 or 2.0 source, e.g. 'OPENQASM 3.0; include "stdgates.inc"; qubit[2] q; bit[2] c; h q[0]; cx q[0], q[1]; c = measure q;'

circuit.description: Alternative to qasm: circuit JSON in format qumo.circuit.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

program.description: Alternative to qasm: program JSON in format qumo.program.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

tools.name: qumo_draw
tools.description:
Use when you need to show a circuit to a person.

Text drawing of a circuit: one line per qubit, columns of gates, @ control, + CX target, x SWAP end, M>c3 measurement into bit 3, ?c0=1 classical condition; detectors, observables and barriers take a whole column. A program draws by blocks, under indented headers. 'style' ascii or unicode; 'width' folds long circuits (0: never).

qasm.description: (required unless circuit is given) OpenQASM 3.0 or 2.0 source, e.g. 'OPENQASM 3.0; include "stdgates.inc"; qubit[2] q; bit[2] c; h q[0]; cx q[0], q[1]; c = measure q;'

circuit.description: Alternative to qasm: circuit JSON in format qumo.circuit.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

program.description: Alternative to qasm: program JSON in format qumo.program.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

tools.name: qumo_convert
tools.description:
Use when you need canonical OpenQASM 3 or circuit JSON from another form.

Convert OpenQASM 2/3 (or circuit JSON) to canonical OpenQASM 3 (to='qasm3', round-trip exact, readable pi fractions), to portable OpenQASM 2 (to='qasm2': qelib1.inc plus exact gate definitions, loads in qiskit.qasm2 strict and legacy modes, pytket and Cirq; needs bound parameters, pass 'params' to bind) or to QUMO circuit JSON (to='json'). A program with runtime control flow goes to OpenQASM 3 or to program JSON (qumo.program.v1); OpenQASM 2 cannot hold it (QM-E585). 'params' binds 'input float' parameters of a circuit before converting.

qasm.description: (required unless circuit is given) OpenQASM 3.0 or 2.0 source, e.g. 'OPENQASM 3.0; include "stdgates.inc"; qubit[2] q; bit[2] c; h q[0]; cx q[0], q[1]; c = measure q;'

circuit.description: Alternative to qasm: circuit JSON in format qumo.circuit.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

program.description: Alternative to qasm: program JSON in format qumo.program.v1 (see qumo_convert to='json')

params.description: Values for 'input float' parameters: array in declaration order or object name->value

tools.name: qumo_transpile
tools.description:
Use when a circuit must run on a target topology and basis, or you want it optimised.
Instead or first: give target as a one-line spec ('grid:4x4/sc_cz', 'heavy_hex:5/rz,sx,x,ecr', 'line:20/u,cx') or edges+basis.
Watch out: level 0-3 picks a preset; 'ai': true is refused for programs with runtime control flow (QM-E630).

Optimize, map and route a circuit for ANY target (vendor-neutral): either a one-line spec 'target' like 'grid:4x4/sc_cz', 'heavy_hex:5/rz,sx,x,ecr', 'trapped_ion:11', 'neutral_atom:4x4', 'line:20/u,cx', or explicit 'edges' [[a,b],...] + 'basis' 'rz,sx,x,cz'. 'level' 0-3 picks a preset; 'ai': true runs the hybrid heuristic + AI preset 'ai_level' 1-3 (learned-policy routing, verified Clifford / linear / permutation / Pauli-network block resynthesis, kept only when cheaper; level 3 is a portfolio with O3); 'pipeline' runs a text pass spec, e.g. 'cancel,merge,fuse1q,route(sabre),basis,cancel'. Returns compiled OpenQASM 3, per-pass report, layouts, swap count and estimated fidelity. A program with runtime control flow compiles block by block on one layout (preset 'level' or 'pipeline'; 'ai' is QM-E630) and is verified: it returns compiled OpenQASM 3, cost per loop, restored SWAPs and how many blocks were checked.

include_program.description: Add the compiled program as qumo.program.v1 JSON

calibration.description: Device data: error_1q, readout, t1_us, t2_us (per qubit), edge_errors [[a, b, e], ...]. Non-uniform data adds post_layout.

angle_bounds.description: Gate name to [min, max], e.g. {"rzz": [0, 1.5708]}. Adds wrap_angles.

tools.name: qumo_estimate_resources
tools.description:
Use when you must decide how or where to run: recommended simulator, memory, NISQ success estimate, fault-tolerant cost.
Instead or first: call before simulating anything above ~20 qubits or before hardware.
Watch out: profile is 'superconducting' | 'trapped_ion' | 'neutral_atom'.

Plan before running: logical metrics (gates, depth, 2q, T-count, Clifford, memory, recommended simulator), NISQ estimate for a modality profile ('superconducting' | 'trapped_ion' | 'neutral_atom': duration, success probability) and a surface-code fault-tolerant estimate (code distance, physical qubits, T factories, runtime) for a physical error rate and error budget.

tools.name: qumo_vqe
tools.description:
Use when you need a ground-state energy of a Pauli-sum Hamiltonian.
Instead or first: set seed; compare with qumo_expectation on the returned circuit if you need a check.

Find the ground-state energy of a Pauli-sum Hamiltonian (e.g. '-1.05*II + 0.39*ZI - 0.39*IZ - 0.01*ZZ + 0.18*XX') with a hardware-efficient ansatz, exact adjoint gradients and BFGS/Adam/SPSA/Nelder-Mead. Deterministic for a seed.

tools.name: qumo_qaoa_maxcut
tools.description:
Use when you solve MaxCut on a small graph given as '0-1 1-2 2-3:0.5'.

Solve MaxCut with depth-p QAOA on a graph given as an edge list '0-1 1-2 2-3:0.5' (optional :weight). Returns expected cut, brute-force optimum, approximation ratio, best sampled bitstring and optimal angles.

tools.name: qumo_qec_memory
tools.description:
Use when you need a logical error rate of a memory experiment for a code, distance, rounds and p.
Instead or first: qumo_qec_dem to inspect the detector error model.
Watch out: set max_errors and shots to bound run time.

Sinter-style logical error rate of a memory experiment: code 'surface_z' | 'surface_x' | 'repetition', distance d, rounds (default d), uniform circuit-level noise p (Stim SI1000-like parameters), decoder 'mwpm' (default: exact minimum-weight perfect matching by sparse blossom, PyMatching 2's algorithm; aliases 'matching', 'pymatching') | 'sparse_blossom' (same decoder) | 'mwpm_correlated' (two-pass reweighting, opt-in: 1.3 to 2.2 times fewer logical errors at d >= 5, worse at d = 3, about 3 times slower) | 'mwpm_dense' (exact MWPM by all-pairs shortest paths + dense blossom; small codes, d <= 5) | 'uf' (union-find; fast, slightly lower threshold) | 'lookup' (lookup table; tiny codes, <= 64 detectors). Bit-packed Pauli-frame sampling; returns logical error rate, std error, Wilson interval, per-round rate, timing and the decoder that ran.

tools.name: qumo_emulate
tools.description:
Use when you want counts under a target device's noise model (T1/T2, gate and readout errors).
Instead or first: compile first with qumo_transpile or set compile=true.

Sample a circuit under the noise of a target (per-qubit T1/T2, 1q and readout errors, per-edge 2q errors, gate durations) without any real device. The circuit must already fit the target (set compile=true to transpile first; QM-E615 otherwise). Takes 'target' or 'edges'+'basis' as qumo_transpile, plus 'calibration' {error_1q, readout, t1_us, t2_us, edge_errors: [[a, b, e], ...]}. Returns counts, the method that ran and the estimated fidelity.

tools.name: qumo_density
tools.description:
Use when noise must be exact (density matrix), up to 15 qubits.
Instead or first: qumo_emulate for larger noisy circuits (sampled).

Exact density-matrix simulation up to 15 qubits: noise is exact, not sampled, and Kraus channels work. Returns outcome probabilities, trace, purity and optionally the expectation of a Pauli sum. Measurements are non-selective; classical conditions raise QM-E411.

tools.name: qumo_to_pbc
tools.description:
Use when you study Pauli-based computation or T-count after commuting Cliffords out.

Litinski's Pauli-based form: commute every Clifford to the end, leaving time-ordered Pauli-product rotations and measurements in the input frame plus one final Clifford. Returns the operations with Pauli strings (highest qubit leftmost), angles in the exp(-i angle/2 P) convention (T = pi/4) and counts: rotations, pi8, arbitrary, measurements, max_weight, layers.

tools.name: qumo_stim_import
tools.description:
Use when you have Stim circuit text to analyse or convert.

Parse Stim circuit text (REPEAT, rec[-k], DETECTOR, OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE, MPP, MX, MR, PAULI_CHANNEL_2, E, ...). Reports sizes and missing_detectors: deterministic measurement parities the circuit does not declare. include_dem adds the detector error model, include_qasm canonical OpenQASM 3.

tools.name: qumo_qec_dem
tools.description:
Use when you need the detector error model (Stim DEM text) of a memory circuit.

Generate a QEC memory circuit and return its detector error model in Stim DEM text ('error(p) D0 D1 L0', with '^' decompositions), optionally the Stim circuit text for cross-checking with Stim/PyMatching.

tools.name: qumo_gpu_info
tools.description:
Use when you need to know whether this build has a usable GPU.

Report whether this QUMO build has GPU support (-D QUMO_GPU) and a usable device: name, API (cuda/hip/metal), vendor, GPU precision ('precision': what precision 'auto' runs, fp32 on every GPU by default like CUDA-Q; 'precision_build_default'; 'precision_env': the QUMO_GPU_PRECISION override; 'precisions': selectable at run time, fp64 only on NVIDIA/AMD; 'precision_note': why), fp64 support, the qubit threshold above which automatic dispatch uses the GPU and the device's tuning profile. Call it before qumo_run_device with device 'gpu'.

tools.name: qumo_run_device
tools.description:
Use when a specific simulator device or precision is required (CPU, NVIDIA, AMD, Apple GPU).
Instead or first: call qumo_gpu_info first to see if a GPU exists.

Like qumo_run_qasm but with an explicit simulator device (vendor-neutral: NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm or Apple Metal through MAX). 'auto' (default) = qumo_run_qasm's dispatch: noisy Clifford circuits without feed-forward -> CPU Pauli frames, other wide/noisy/dynamic Clifford circuits -> stabilizer tableau, static non-Clifford circuits with >= 16 qubits -> GPU state vector when this build has GPU support (-D QUMO_GPU) and a usable device (CPU on any GPU failure), everything else -> CPU state vector. 'cpu' = the same choice restricted to CPU simulators. 'gpu' = Clifford circuits without parameters or classical feed-forward (noise, mid-circuit measurement and reset allowed) -> GPU Pauli frames ('gpu:pauli_frame'); other static, noiseless circuits -> GPU state vector in 'precision' ('gpu:statevector:fp32' or 'gpu:statevector:fp64'); dynamic or noisy non-Clifford circuits, builds without -D QUMO_GPU, or no usable device -> run on the CPU as with 'cpu' plus warning QM-W020 giving the reason. 'precision' (GPU state vector only): 'auto' (default: QUMO_GPU_PRECISION when set, else the build default, fp32 on every GPU as in CUDA-Q), 'fp32', or 'fp64' (NVIDIA/AMD; error QM-E472 on Apple GPUs, which have no fp64); CPU simulators are fp64 (warning QM-W021 when a requested precision did not apply). Returns counts, 'method' (the simulator that ran), 'device_used', 'precision_used' and structured 'warnings'.

max_iterations.description: Loop back-edges allowed per shot; past it the run stops with QM-E480

params.description: Values for 'input float' parameters: array in declaration order or object name->value

precision.description: GPU state-vector precision: auto = QUMO_GPU_PRECISION or the build default (fp32)

tools.name: qumo_build_circuit
tools.description:
Use when a standard algorithm is wanted (ghz, qft, grover, bernstein_vazirani, deutsch_jozsa, qaoa_maxcut, hea, uccsd, trotter, kernels).
Instead or first: use it instead of writing gates by hand; pass its OpenQASM to the simulators.
Watch out: unknown kinds or arguments are refused (QM-E801/QM-E802); parameterised output needs 'params' when simulated.

Build a circuit from QUMO's algorithm library by name instead of writing gates: ghz, qft, iqft, grover (marked bitstrings), bernstein_vazirani, deutsch_jozsa, qaoa_maxcut (edge-list graph, depth p), hea (hardware-efficient ansatz), uccsd, h2_ansatz, trotter (Pauli-sum Hamiltonian), reuploading_classifier (data re-uploading QML classifier), angle_kernel (compute-uncompute quantum kernel). Returns OpenQASM 3 with symbolic parameters as 'input float' (or OpenQASM 2 for parameter-free circuits), parameter names in order, gate counts, two-qubit gates, depth, the observable to measure (MaxCut cost, molecular or given Hamiltonian) and notes. Sizes are capped; unknown arguments are rejected (QM-E801/QM-E802).

args.description: Kind-specific arguments: ghz {n}; qft/iqft {n, do_swaps, approximation_degree}; grover {marked: [bitstrings], iterations}; bernstein_vazirani {secret: bitstring}; deutsch_jozsa {n, balanced_mask, constant_value}; qaoa_maxcut {graph: '0-1 1-2:0.5', p}; hea {n, layers, entanglement, rotations, hamiltonian}; uccsd {num_qubits, num_electrons, singles, doubles, hamiltonian}; h2_ansatz {}; trotter {hamiltonian, time, steps, order, num_qubits, param_name}; reuploading_classifier {n, layers, num_features}; angle_kernel {n, rotation}

measure.description: Append measurements (search/input qubits only for grover, bernstein_vazirani, deutsch_jozsa)

format.description: qasm2 needs a circuit without symbolic parameters

tools.name: qumo_ft_codes
tools.description:
Use when you need QUMO's stabilizer codes for fault-tolerant programs.

List QUMO's stabilizer codes for fault-tolerant programming (Steane [[7,1,3]], Iceberg [[k+2,k,2]], [[4,2,2]] CSS and non-CSS, [[5,1,3]], surface and repetition adapters) with generators, logical operators, CSS flag and a brute-force distance check; with 'architecture' ('steane' | 'iceberg_<k>') also describe the architecture (logical gate set, QEC policy, factories) and verify every gadget of its library with the stabilizer tableau (and state vector for magic states).

code.description: steane, five_qubit, css_422, noncss_422, iceberg_<k>, surface_<d>, repetition_<d>

tools.name: qumo_ft_encode
tools.description:
Use when you want to encode a logical circuit on a code and sample it with noise.
Instead or first: qumo_ft_codes first to choose the code.

Encode a QEC-agnostic circuit (any gates, mid-circuit measurement, reset, c_if feed-forward) into a fault-tolerant physical program, Guppy FT style: compile (computational -> logical gate set of the architecture: Steane Clifford+T with magic-state injection and static Clifford+T or comparator RUS synthesis of Rz, or Iceberg native rotations) then implement_ops (logical -> physical gadgets, block allocation, state factories, QEC-cycle policy, Pauli-frame feed-forward, decoding). Returns the logical program summary, a resource report (physical qubits, depth, 2q gates, QEC cycles, magic states) and, with 'shots', the encoded program emulated next to the unencoded reference (optional circuit-level noise 'noise_p').

tools.name: qumo_ft_verify
tools.description:
Use when you must prove a physical gadget implements a logical operation exactly.

Check that a physical gadget implements a logical operation on a stabilizer code, exactly, with the stabilizer tableau: kind 'clifford' (semantic Clifford on num_blocks*k qubits vs unitary implementation on num_blocks*n (+ clean ancillas): stabilizers preserved and logical Paulis mapped with the right signs) or 'state' (stabilizer-state preparation, flags/measurements allowed, accept branch). Returns valid + the first failing operator.
